references.text: The same procedure of washing the entrails and feet with water, and the priest burns it on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord - parallel instruction for cattle.
Moses washed the entrails and feet with water and burned the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
Aaron washed the entrails and feet and burned them together with the burnt offering on the altar.
Instructions to wash the entrails and feet, and burn the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Conclusion of the instructions regarding bird offerings, which are also an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The first time the expression 'a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (ריח ניחח) is used in Scripture, when Noah offered burnt offerings.
Paul uses sacrificial terminology and describes Christ's sacrifice as a pleasing aroma to God (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας).
Both verses confirm that regardless of the type of offering, it is 'the offering made by fire' that creates the pleasant fragrance accepted by the Lord.
Both verses define the burning of the sacrifice as a 'food' or 'offering made by fire' that produces the pleasing aroma for the Lord.
Both verses demonstrate that even for sin offerings, it is the burning of the fat that creates the 'pleasing aroma' which triggers God's acceptance.
The connection shows that the principle of 'a pleasing aroma' through burning is universal for both animal and grain offerings.
